head: HEAD
description:
Review the bundled demo shop's user-visible cart and checkout behavior. Exercise adding
a widget and completing an ordinary purchase. Also examine the expired-card path, which
the repository describes as a known defect, while distinguishing an expected payment
rejection from an unrelated application or browser failure.

journeys.title: Add a widget to the cart and complete an ordinary purchase
journeys.goal: Add a widget to the cart and pay with a valid card to receive a confirmed order.
journeys.because: The demo's own e2e suite (test_add_item_to_cart, test_checkout_with_valid_card) treats add-to-cart plus a successful checkout as the core happy path, and ui.py exposes the same flow through browser forms at /ui, /ui/cart/items and /ui/checkout.

state: Shop has been reset via POST /reset so the catalog and carts start empty

steps.do: Navigate to /ui in a fresh unauthenticated browser.
steps.see: The shop page loads with a product form offering a Product select (including a 'widget' option), a Quantity input, and a submit control.

steps.do: Select 'widget' as the product, leave quantity at 1, and submit the form.
steps.see: The browser is taken to a cart page showing the widget listed as a line item with its price and a total reflecting one widget.

steps.do: On the cart page, submit the checkout form with the 'valid' card token.
steps.see: A confirmation page is shown with the text 'Order confirmed' and an order reference value.

journeys.title: Checkout with a declined card is rejected but the cart survives for retry
journeys.persona: Shopper whose card is declined at checkout
journeys.goal: Attempt checkout with a card token that the payment step rejects, and confirm the shopper can still see and retry their cart.
journeys.because: ui.py's ui_checkout handler and app.py's submit_checkout both special-case the 'declined' token as an expected payment rejection that intentionally preserves the cart so the shopper can retry with another card, distinguishing it from the expired-card defect below.

state: Shop has been reset via POST /reset so carts start empty

steps.do: Navigate to /ui and add one widget to the cart via the product form.
steps.see: A cart page appears listing the widget and its total.

steps.do: On the cart page, submit the checkout form using the 'declined' card token.
steps.see: The cart page reloads showing the alert message 'Card was declined.' instead of an order confirmation.

steps.do: Reload the cart page for the same cart id.
steps.see: The widget item is still present in the cart with its total unchanged, confirming the decline preserved the cart for a retry.

journeys.traces_to: ui.py:120 (/ui/checkout, declined branch), app.py:123 (/checkout/submit, declined branch)

journeys.title: Checkout with an expired card surfaces the documented defect: generic message and cleared cart
journeys.persona: Shopper whose card has expired at checkout
journeys.goal: Attempt checkout with an expired card token and observe both the correct payment rejection and the two documented defects: the message never names the card as expired, and the cart is cleared unlike a plain decline.
journeys.because: ui.py explicitly comments this as a DELIBERATE DEFECT (demo): the expired-card path returns a generic 'Payment failed.' message that never names the card as expired, and clears the cart unlike the 'declined' path -- the change description asks to distinguish this expected payment rejection from an unrelated application/browser failure while still recording the known defect.

state: Shop has been reset via POST /reset so carts start empty

steps.do: Navigate to /ui and add one widget to the cart via the product form.
steps.see: A cart page appears listing the widget and its total.

steps.do: On the cart page, submit the checkout form using the 'expired' card token.
steps.see: The page reloads as 'Your cart' showing the alert message 'Payment failed.' (a correct payment rejection, but the message does not mention that the card expired).

steps.do: Observe the cart contents shown on that same reloaded page.
steps.see: The cart is now empty (0 items, total 0), unlike the declined-card path which preserves the cart -- this is the documented CHANGE-type defect.

journeys.traces_to: ui.py:120-149 (/ui/checkout, expired branch, DELIBERATE DEFECT comment), app.py:123-154 (/checkout/submit, expired branch)

journeys.title: Checkout against a cart id the shop does not recognize is rejected
journeys.persona: Shopper (or stale browser tab) submitting checkout for a cart that no longer exists
journeys.goal: Confirm that submitting the checkout form with an unrecognized cart id produces a clear rejection rather than a crash.
journeys.because: ui_checkout in ui.py explicitly checks 'if cart_id not in state.carts' and returns a 'We could not find that cart.' alert, an alternate user-visible entry point worth exercising separately from the payment-rejection paths.

state: Shop has been reset via POST /reset

steps.do: Navigate directly to /ui/cart/does-not-exist in the browser (simulating a stale or bookmarked cart link).
steps.see: A cart page is rendered for the unknown id (per ui_cart handler behavior).

steps.do: Submit a checkout POST for that same nonexistent cart id with the 'valid' card token (e.g. via any checkout form pointed at that cart id).
steps.see: The page shows the alert 'We could not find that cart.' instead of an order confirmation.

unresolved: No documented command, working directory, or entrypoint was found in the provided evidence for launching the demo shop as a persistent HTTP server (server.py only shows an ephemeral-port context manager used by tests, not a CLI invocation); the 'command' field is left blank pending clarification.
No required environment variables were found in the cited evidence, so required_env is empty; confirm none are needed to start the demo app.

The e2e test file hardcodes BASE_URL = 'http://127.0.0.1:8000', implying the app is normally served on port 8000, but no source instructs how that port/host is fixed for a manual run; health_url and reset_command assume that convention and should be confirmed.

ui.py's GET /ui/cart/{cart_id} handler content for an unknown cart id was truncated in the excerpt; the exact wording shown to the shopper when navigating directly to a nonexistent cart id (versus only on checkout) is not fully confirmed.

sources.ui.py: Defines the browser-facing routes /ui, /ui/cart/items, /ui/cart/{cart_id}, /ui/cart/{cart_id}/remove, and /ui/checkout, including the declined vs. expired card handling and the DELIBERATE DEFECT comment describing the expired-card bug.
sources.app.py: Defines the JSON API state machine (ShopState, CATALOG, CARD_TOKENS) and endpoints /cart/items, /cart/{cart_id}, /checkout/submit, /health, /reset that the UI layer wraps; confirms declined vs. expired behavior parity with the UI.
sources.server.py: Shows the app is served via uvicorn over a real socket for browser-realistic runs, but only as a context-managed ephemeral-port helper, not a standalone launch command.
sources.e2e/test_shop_flows.py: Human-written e2e suite treating add-to-cart, valid checkout, and expired-card checkout as the flows worth protecting; also documents BASE_URL http://127.0.0.1:8000 convention and the /reset endpoint used for a fresh state precondition.
